decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'Add, edit, delete... bookmarks'; round 1 client confirms 'the save-and-manage flow is here' and could add a bookmark. Round 2 client: 'I can easily save links and keep them managed'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Core save/edit/delete present and conforming to reference; no divergence from these items.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker presents 'Add... bookmarks' with no auto-metadata; round 1 client: 'When I went to add a bookmark, it asks me to type in the title (and a note) myself... Can you make it so that pasting a URL pulls in the page's title and details automatically? I can still tweak them afterward'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Divergence established independently: presented add flow requires manual title entry, contradicting REF-BM-02 (auto-collect title/description). Client rejects the mismatch and supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (auto-populate on paste, still editable per REF-BM-03) → corrective/correct.

decisions.evidence: round 2 maker: 'Fetches the page title and description' (only); no favicon or preview image mentioned. Round 2 client: 'it pulled in the page's title and description on its own, and I could still edit them... I'm happy with this.'
decisions.note: Implementation review (revised presentation of REF-BM-02, a new decision at a later point). Delivered auto-collection covers only title/description; REF-BM-02 also requires favicon and preview image, which remain absent. Client approves without expressing the difference → unexpressed_divergence.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'Search across titles, notes, domains, and tags'; round 1/2 client references 'search' approvingly ('search, favorites, sorting').
decisions.note: Prototype review. Full-text search over title/note/domain(url)/tags is functionally equivalent to REF-BM-12; treated as conforming. Advanced operators (REF-BM-13..16) were never presented or discussed, so no decision is fabricated for them.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'Alphabetical and newest-first sorting'; round 2 client lists 'sorting' among what works.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Sort by title (alphabetical) and date added (newest-first) conforms to REF-BM-22.

decisions.evidence: round 1 maker: 'Grid and list layouts'; round 1 client: 'the grid/list views... clean'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. List/grid display exposing bookmark items is a functionally equivalent realisation of REF-BM-07 (readability-first list); layout style is an orthogonal UI choice.
